method: Exactly two ordinary terminal attempts on normal http://127.0.0.1:5173/ through existing visible driver, visible handbook/brief and HUD/JPEG evidence only. No source, tests, hidden state, arranged positions, or other browser tools. Software-WebGL fallback; no hardware certification.

attempts.coverage: Reached return-to-extraction phase, died near north area before uplink. West then east then Heart.
Reached uplink deck and HOLD THE EXTRACTION ZONE. HUD response before capture was 65%, JPEG visibly 67%; died before automatic pause, terminal confirmed. No successful extraction.

observations: Strong rain-soaked cyan/amber visual identity, polished title and outcome typography, clear rifle silhouette and strong Heart landmark. Repeated simple robot forms and broad flat concrete/storage geometry still read as a vertical slice rather than AAA production.
Core recovery supplies visibly restored health, armor and reserve ammunition; changing route on replay was useful. Objective shift and green uplink progress were clear.
Brief and handbook explain console proximity, pausing map, charge cancel, shield regeneration and capacitor hazards thoroughly. Onscreen control strip omits sprint, though handbook includes it.
Paused facility map was legible and useful for route planning. Storage and low-cover collisions caused repeated route corrections and consumed health; a jump over east low cover visibly worked.

Thin small HUD text, overlapping world signage/markers and signal-behind-cover notes became busy. Charging/recent-fire cues exposed threats but several simultaneous directions were difficult to act on through intermittent captures.

Shooting the entry optic produced critical elimination feedback. Second run also eliminated Heart warden by firing while recovering. Most guards remained alive, creating substantial return/extraction pressure; my low accuracy and route errors contributed to both deaths.

Uplink deck asks movement within deck and has split baffles. Second run entered at low health, remained relatively exposed and died at roughly two-thirds upload. This does not establish extraction balance or a defect.
